quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #11
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 28

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and hazards. This sign warns you that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of traffic light colors?
questions.explanation: On a vertical traffic light, red is always at the top and green is always at the bottom. On a horizontal traffic light, red is always on the left and green is always on the right.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private driveway?

options.text: Honk your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out quickly to merge with traffic.
Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and traffic on the roadway go first.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works like:
questions.explanation: At a flashing red light, you must stop and let all traffic that doesn't have to stop go first.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." What does this mean?

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next speed limit sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down before the reduced speed zone.
You should only reduce speed to 35 mph in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: "Reduced speed" signs tell drivers to slow down. The new speed limit begins right at the sign.

questions.question: You must signal every time you pull away from a curb.
questions.explanation: You must use your turn signal every time you pull away from a curb.

questions.question: It starts to sleet or snow while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Keep your windshield and mirrors clear.
Stay farther away from the vehicles you are following.
Drive carefully around all other vehicles.

questions.explanation: In snow, keep your windshield and mirrors clear. Increase the space between your car and the car ahead because wet, icy roads make it harder to stop.

questions.question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
Some drivers must yield to others.
You must drive below the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Regulatory signs that forbid actions are rectangular with white backgrounds and red and black markings. A red circle and slash over a black symbol means that action is not allowed.

questions.question: You are entering a busy freeway. How should you merge into traffic?

options.text: Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder for blind spots.
Use the on-ramp to match the speed of freeway traffic.
Let traffic already on the freeway go first.

questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up to match freeway traffic and let traffic already on the freeway go first. Check your mirrors and blind spots before merging to make sure you have room to merge safely.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot before changing lanes?

options.text: Look in the left side mirror.
Look in the right side mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.
questions.explanation: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.

questions.question: To be ready for what is ahead on the road, you should:

options.text: Look at the whole road and roadsides continuously.
Look straight ahead at all times.
Drive with your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Keep your focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the whole road and roadsides continuously.
questions.explanation: You can handle dangerous situations better if you look ahead and find problems before you reach them. Do not just stare at the center of the road. Look at the entire road, including both sides.

questions.question: Driving at night using only parking lights is against the law.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive at night using only parking lights. You must use your headlights when driving in the dark.

questions.question: Any amount of alcohol in the blood may affect a driver's:
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol can affect your ability to drive safely. Any alcohol can hurt your judgment and physical coordination. Driving after drinking even a small amount can result in criminal charges.

questions.question: Which describes how defensive drivers think?

options.text: They know other drivers will do the right thing.
They expect what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
They expect nothing and give nothing to other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They expect what other drivers might do and are ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means thinking ahead about what others might do wrong and being ready to respond to their mistakes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare that makes it hard to see.

questions.question: If a traffic light is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:

options.text: Do what the car in front of you does.

questions.explanation: You must obey a police officer's directions, even if they conflict with traffic signals, signs, or road markings.

questions.question: After passing a vehicle, it is safe to move back to the right lane:

options.text: When you cannot see the passed vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the whole front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the whole front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, move back to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean:

options.text: Do not pass from either direction.
You can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either side. You may only cross these lines to turn left or to pass pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter riders when the opposite lane is clear.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a crossroad is coming.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, you must:

options.text: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go, then proceed.
Slow down and proceed with caution.
Stop completely and stay stopped while the light is red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely, let oncoming traffic and pedestrians go, then proceed.
questions.explanation: Treat a flashing red light like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and go when it is safe.

questions.question: Backing your vehicle is:

options.text: Dangerous if you have a helper.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see clearly behind your vehicle. Use extra caution when backing up.

questions.question: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest you can drive in an area.
questions.explanation: The posted maximum speed limit is the fastest legal speed in an area under good conditions. You must slow down when conditions are bad, such as wet roads or poor visibility.

questions.question: An octagonal sign is always a:
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs are always stop signs. Come to a complete stop when you see a red, eight-sided sign.

questions.question: You should increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead when you:

options.text: Are following a small passenger vehicle.
Are being tailgated by another driver.
Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are being tailgated by another driver.
questions.explanation: When another driver is tailgating you, create extra space in front of your vehicle. Slow down gradually or move to another lane to prevent a collision.

questions.question: To help others see you when daylight begins to fade, you should use your:
questions.explanation: As daylight fades, turn on your low beam headlights so others can see you. Use high beam headlights only when driving in open areas with no other vehicles.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is ahead.

questions.question: A red traffic signal light means that you must:
questions.explanation: A red light means you must stop before entering the intersection. You must also stop at any stop line and before entering any crosswalk.

questions.question: What does an orange-colored sign indicate?

options.text: The start of a no passing zone.

questions.explanation: Orange signs with black symbols warn of construction, maintenance, and emergency work ahead.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a two-lane road indicates:

options.text: Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Solid lines mean you cannot pass.

questions.question: When driving on slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Drive as you would on dry roads.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead. Your vehicle will need more time to stop.

questions.question: Your power steering stops working while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn and turn off the engine.
Turn on your hazard lights and brace yourself.
Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer firmly, slow down, drive to a safe area, and stop.
questions.explanation: Without power steering, you need to use more force to steer. Slow down and pull off the road to a safe area before stopping.

questions.question: When turning left, you have the right-of-way with which traffic light?
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can go in that direction. Oncoming traffic must stop for you.

questions.question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?

options.text: When there is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.
When the railroad crossing is in a city or town with frequent train traffic.
When you are carrying two or more young children in your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is not enough space on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.
questions.explanation: A train can come on any track at any time, going either direction. Make sure your entire vehicle is past the tracks before you stop.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line on a highway mean?

options.text: You cannot cross the line to pass.
You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: A dashed white line means you can cross it to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What should a driver always do?

options.text: Assume all drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers obey right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Always be prepared to yield if it can prevent a crash.
